forensic_metrics.financial: Cost delta analysis of external vs internal monitor ($50-$100 impact); Evaluation of ALPS faders ($15) vs Penny & Giles for cost reduction/retrofit

forensic_metrics.governance: Cross-functional 'Digi-Buckley' meetings; Sustaining D-Control issues email group created for production assembly feedback

forensic_summary.trigger: Flagship console launch to replace ProControl; Critical tolerance accumulation issues in modular 16/32 fader configurations causing assembly failures
forensic_summary.intervention: Erik Norris 'rigidified' sheet metal structure; Implemented 'ratcheting compression strap' assembly method to force unit alignment; Manual 'tweaking' of warped fader pans during assembly
forensic_summary.result: Successful launch of D-Control (Buckley) and D-Command (Danko); TEC Award nomination

war_stories.label: The Bowed Fader Pan
war_stories.description: PEM hardware insertion stretched sheet metal, causing an 'arch' or 'bow' from front to back, requiring manual bending to fix.

war_stories.label: The Cracked End Cap
war_stories.description: Plastic end caps cracking due to interference with screw heads and torque stress; resolved by ECO to increase hole diameters.

war_stories.label: The V-2 Tinderbox
war_stories.description: Discovery that PCBs were manufactured with V-2 material (flammable) instead of V-0, described as 'a virtual tinderbox' relative to spec.

isomorphics.label: Tolerance Stack-up
isomorphics.hardware_point: Multiplying effect on tolerance error due to length/width of multiple unit assemblies (Main + Fader)
isomorphics.software_point: Firmware updates required to support different fader orientations (ALPS vs P&G)

toolchain: Vendors: Mass Precision (Sheet Metal), Jetcrown (Plastics), PPI Plastics, Alps, Penny & Giles

I am ready, willing and able to implement. I just need resolution. There are time/cost constraints mandating judgment calls that are way above my head.

The difference between an acceptable unit and failing unit is actually smaller than is advertised. I think this is due to the multiplying effect on tolerance error due to the length and width of each unit.
